html:
Navratri is right around the corner, bringing nine nights of vibrant Garba, family gatherings, and traditional fasting. For many of us in Gujarat, vrat is a deeply cherished spiritual practice. But if you or a loved one is living with Type 2 diabetes, the festive season can feel like a delicate balancing act.

It is very natural to think that fasting results in reduced levels of blood sugar, but the reality is different. Traditional vrat menus that include deep-fried sabudana tikkis, potato wafers, and the sugary dessert kheer could be a cause of high glucose levels. On the other hand, fasting for several hours can lead to hypoglycaemia (low blood sugar).

Before starting your fast, consult a skilled diabetes specialist in Ahmedabad at Silver Touch Hospitals to review your medication timings and daily glucose targets.

Here is how you can observe your fast safely while keeping your energy high for Garba.

Swap Pure Starches for Low-GI Flours

Sabudana, or tapioca, is responsible for most of the sugar surge after meals due to its high starch content. However, you can opt for low-GI flours, which release their energy slowly:

  • Rajgira (Amaranth): Rich in protein and dietary fibre, making it the best option for vrat rotis or cheelas.
  • Kuttu (Buckwheat) & Singhara (Water Chestnut): These flours offer complex carbohydrates. Use them with minimal oil rather than deep-frying puris.

Never Skip Protein and Fibre

In order to avoid blood sugar from increasing once you have broken your fast, include proteins and fats along with carbohydrates in your diet. Include roasted peanuts, paneer, and curd in your diet. A plate of roasted makhana or even almonds is a much better choice for evening snacks than those packet potato chips.

Eat Small, Frequent Portions

It is a mistake to starve throughout the day and indulge yourself in just one big meal after sunset, as it confuses your metabolism. Have smaller meals throughout the day in three or four portions. If you feel lightheaded, sweating, and very tired during Garba, test your blood sugar levels right away. Don’t forget to carry a fast-acting glucose source with you.
